title: Los Angeles Trivia Night

questions.q: Translated from Spanish, what does the name "Los Angeles" mean?
When the Hollywood Sign went up in 1923, it carried which four extra letters on the end?
Which baseball team moved to Los Angeles from Brooklyn in 1958?
Ice Age fossils, including saber-toothed cats, are still dug out of which sticky pits in Hancock Park?
Which Los Angeles stadium hosted the Summer Olympics in both 1932 and 1984?
The Hollywood Walk of Fame runs along Hollywood Boulevard and which cross street?
The Lakers kept their name from the state they played in before moving west. Which state?
Which architect designed the curving stainless steel Walt Disney Concert Hall downtown?
Stars have left what in the wet cement of the forecourt at the TCL (formerly Grauman's) Chinese Theatre?
Which university, whose teams are the Bruins, has its campus in Westwood?

notes: Spanish 'los ángeles' = 'the angels', from the founding name El Pueblo de Nuestra Señora la Reina de los Ángeles; see Los Angeles (Wikipedia), Etymology.
Erected 1923 as HOLLYWOODLAND; the LAND letters were removed in 1949; see Hollywood Sign (Wikipedia) or hollywoodsign.org.
Dodgers played their first Los Angeles season in 1958 after leaving Brooklyn; see Los Angeles Dodgers (Wikipedia) or MLB.com.
La Brea Tar Pits in Hancock Park, Smilodon among the fossils; see La Brea Tar Pits (Wikipedia) or tarpits.org (Natural History Museum of LA County).
Memorial Coliseum was main stadium for the 1932 and 1984 Summer Olympics; see Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum (Wikipedia) or lacoliseum.com.
Walk of Fame covers Hollywood Boulevard and Vine Street; see Hollywood Walk of Fame (Wikipedia) or walkoffame.com.
Minneapolis Lakers, named for Minnesota's 'Land of 10,000 Lakes', moved to LA in 1960; see Los Angeles Lakers (Wikipedia) or NBA.com.
Walt Disney Concert Hall (opened 2003) designed by Frank Gehry; see Walt Disney Concert Hall (Wikipedia) or laphil.com.
Forecourt of the Stars with hand and footprints in cement since 1927; see TCL Chinese Theatre (Wikipedia).
UCLA Bruins, campus in Westwood; see University of California, Los Angeles (Wikipedia) or ucla.edu.
